probes.name: long text is clamped to the byte cap
a clamped string announces the cut
NaN maxBytes throws
probes.derivation: NaN is not an integer, so a guard written as `Number.isInteger(maxBytes) && maxBytes > 0` rejects it — but a guard written as a remainder or comparison test (`maxBytes % 1 === 0`, `!(maxBytes < 1)`) ACCEPTS NaN and then silently returns the whole text. Pristine: no throw.

probes.name: Infinity maxBytes throws
probes.derivation: Infinity is not an integer either, and passes any `> 0` test. Pristine: no throw (buf.length <= Infinity, returns the text).

probes.name: undefined maxBytes throws
probes.derivation: the prompt says non-numbers must all throw. Pristine: no throw (buf.length <= undefined is false, so it falls into the truncation path).

probes.name: true maxBytes throws
probes.derivation: a boolean is a non-number that coerces to 1, so an unguarded comparison treats `true` as a 1-byte cap. Pristine: no throw.

probes.name: false maxBytes throws
probes.derivation: coerces to 0 — the same class as the explicit 0 probe, reached by a different route. Pristine: no throw.

probes.name: empty text with an invalid cap still throws
probes.derivation: pristine clampText("", 0, "probe") returns "" because 0 <= 0 takes the early return. A guard placed AFTER that early return therefore never fires here — this probe is what forces it to the head of the function.

probes.name: cap 1 truncates to one byte
probes.derivation: pristine clampText("hi", 1, "probe") → "h": 2 bytes > 1, the notice does not fit in 1 byte (room < 0), so the documented silent cut applies. A valid positive integer must keep behaving exactly as before, so this is pinned to the pristine value.

probes.name: a very large cap returns the text unchanged
probes.derivation: pristine clampText("hi", 2147483647, "probe") → "hi". 2147483647 is a positive integer, so a guard that rejects large caps (an arbitrary upper bound) fails here.

probes.name: empty text with a valid cap returns ""
probes.derivation: pristine clampText("", 10, "probe") → "" (0 bytes <= 10). Confirms the new guard did not turn the empty-string case into a throw for VALID caps.

probes.name: multibyte truncation cuts on a character boundary
probes.derivation: pristine clampText("日本語テキスト", 12, "probe") → "日本語テ" — 7 chars x 3 bytes = 21 bytes, the notice does not fit in 12, and 12 bytes is exactly 4 characters. EXACT content, so a truncation that merely fits the cap does not pass.

probes.name: multibyte truncation backs off a split sequence
probes.derivation: pristine clampText("日本語テキスト", 11, "probe") → "日本語" (9 bytes): 11 bytes would split the fourth character, so the strict decoder backs up to 9. This is the branch the byte-cap probes alone never reach.
